title: Finite type algebras over G-rings are G-rings
statement: Let $R$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. If $R\to S$ is of finite type, meaning that $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra (equivalently, a quotient of $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$), then $S$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PV).

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PV (tag 07PV, label proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07PV; the proposition states the finite type case used here, and its proof reduces to polynomial extensions and localizations. It is invoked by Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX), item (5).

proof.text: (Reduction to $R[x]$.) Since $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra, there are $n\ge0$ and a surjective $R$-algebra map $P_n=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to S$, so $S\cong P_n/J$ for an ideal $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-quotient] it suffices to show that $P_n$ is a G-ring. As $P_0=R$ and $P_k=P_{k-1}[x_k]$ is the polynomial ring in one variable over $P_{k-1}$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], by induction on $n$ it suffices to prove: (*) if $R$ is a G-ring, then $R[x]$ is a G-ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), first paragraph (lines 12555-12560): 'Writing S as a quotient of R[x_1,...,x_n] we see from Lemma 07PP that it suffices to prove that R[x_1,...,x_n] is a G-ring. By induction on n it suffices to prove that R[x] is a G-ring.' (Stacks first reduces 'essentially of finite type' to finite type by localization; for the finite type statement here that reduction is not needed.)

proof.text: (Reduction to maximal ideals.) Let $R$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; it is Noetherian, so $R[x]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-maximal-ideal-criterion] it suffices to show that for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset R[x]$ the completion map $R[x]_{\mathfrak q}\to(R[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12560-12566: 'Let q in R[x] be a maximal ideal. By Lemma 07PT it suffices to show that R[x]_q -> R[x]_q^ is regular.'

proof.text: (Reduction to a local base.) Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset R[x]$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, a prime of $R$, $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] (applied to the identity of $R$) $A$ is a Noetherian local ring, and by the definition of a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] its completion map $A\to A^\wedge$ is regular. Let $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, viewed in $R[x]$; then $A[x]=W^{-1}(R[x])$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. As $W\cap\mathfrak q=\emptyset$, $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak qA[x]$ is a prime of $A[x]$ with $\mathfrak Q\cap R[x]=\mathfrak q$, and $\mathfrak Q\cap A=\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak m$. Moreover $A[x]/\mathfrak Q$ is the localization of the field $R[x]/\mathfrak q$ at the image of $W$, which does not contain $0$, so $A[x]/\mathfrak Q=R[x]/\mathfrak q$ is a field and $\mathfrak Q$ is maximal. Since $W\subseteq R[x]\setminus\mathfrak q$, both $A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$ and $R[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ are the localization of $R[x]$ at $R[x]\setminus\mathfrak q$, compatibly with the maximal ideals, hence also $(A[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge=(R[x]_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$. So it suffices to prove: (**) if $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a Noetherian local ring whose completion map $A\to A^\wedge$ is regular and $\mathfrak Q\subset A[x]$ is a maximal ideal with $\mathfrak Q\cap A=\mathfrak m$, then $c:A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}\to(A[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge$ is regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12566-12569: 'If q lies over p in R, then we may replace R by R_p. Hence we may assume that R is a Noetherian local G-ring with maximal ideal m and that q lies over m.' (Only the regularity of R_p -> R_p^ is used below, so the G-ring property of R_p is not needed.)

proof.text: (The prime $\mathfrak Q'$.) Put $B=A^\wedge$, the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $\iota:A\to B$. Then $B$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mB$ and $A/\mathfrak m\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak mB$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and $\mathfrak mB$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] ($\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated); $B[x]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $\iota[x]:A[x]\to B[x]=B\otimes_AA[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. It induces $A[x]/\mathfrak mA[x]=(A/\mathfrak m)[x]\xrightarrow{\sim}(B/\mathfrak mB)[x]=B[x]/\mathfrak mB[x]$, so contraction along $\iota[x]$ is a bijection from the primes of $B[x]$ containing $\mathfrak mB[x]$ onto the primes of $A[x]$ containing $\mathfrak mA[x]$. Every prime of $B[x]$ over $\mathfrak Q$ contains $\mathfrak QB[x]\supseteq\mathfrak mB[x]$; hence there is exactly one prime $\mathfrak Q'\subset B[x]$ with $\iota[x]^{-1}(\mathfrak Q')=\mathfrak Q$, $B[x]/\mathfrak Q'\cong A[x]/\mathfrak Q$ is a field, so $\mathfrak Q'$ is maximal, and $\mathfrak Q'\cap B\supseteq\mathfrak mB$ is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak mB$ of $B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12569-12571: 'Note that there is a unique prime q' in R^[x] lying over q.' (the argument is not written in Stacks and is written out here)

proof.text: (Lower arrow.) $\iota:A\to B$ is regular by (**)'s hypothesis and $A\to A[x]$ is of finite type, so the base change $\iota[x]:A[x]\to B\otimes_AA[x]=B[x]$ is regular [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change]. Since $B[x]$ is Noetherian and $\iota[x]^{-1}(\mathfrak Q')=\mathfrak Q$, the induced map of localizations $\psi:A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}\to B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'}$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] ((1)$\Rightarrow$(2)). In particular $\psi$ is flat, and it is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12580-12582: 'Since R is a G-ring the lower horizontal arrow is regular (as a localization of a base change of the regular ring map R -> R^).' Base change: Lemma Tag 07C1; localization: Lemma Tag 07C0.

proof.text: (Right arrow and composite.) Applying [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-complete-local-formal-fibres] to the Noetherian complete local ring $(B,\mathfrak mB)$ and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak Q'\subset B[x]$ with $\mathfrak Q'\cap B=\mathfrak mB$ (Step 4), the completion map $c':B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'}\to(B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'})^\wedge$ is regular. The ring $(B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'})^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], so all fibre rings of $c'\circ\psi$ are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], and $c'\circ\psi:A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}\to(B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'})^\wedge$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12583-12590: 'Suppose we can prove the right vertical arrow is regular. Then it follows that the composition ... is regular' (Lemma Tag 07QI); the right vertical arrow is the complete case, lines 12592-12637.

proof.text: (Descent to the left arrow.) Let $\psi^\wedge:(A[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge\to(B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'})^\wedge$ be the map of completions induced by the flat local homomorphism $\psi$, so that $\psi^\wedge\circ c=c'\circ\psi$; it is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion]. Both completions are local with maximal ideals generated by the maximal ideals of $A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$, $B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], so $\psi^\wedge$ is a flat local homomorphism and $\operatorname{Spec}$ of it is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence] to $A[x]_{\mathfrak Q}\xrightarrow{c}(A[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge\xrightarrow{\psi^\wedge}(B[x]_{\mathfrak Q'})^\wedge$, whose composite $c'\circ\psi$ is regular by Step 6, $c$ is regular. This proves (**), hence (*) by Step 3 and Step 2, hence the proposition by Step 1.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, line 12552), lines 12587-12591: '... and hence the left vertical arrow is regular by Lemma 07NT. Hence we see that we may assume R is a Noetherian complete local ring and q a prime lying over the maximal ideal of R.' Flatness and Spec-surjectivity of the map of completions, implicit in Stacks, via Tags 0C4G and 00HR.
